subject: blister beetle
title: Hundreds of Beetle Larvae Pile Up to Fake a Female Bee

scenes.text: A male bee tries to mate with this lump.
It's a clump of beetle larvae. From 120 to over 2,000 of them, on one stem.
Together they copy the scent of a female bee. Males can't resist.
The moment he touches down, the larvae grab on. It takes under two seconds.
When he finds a real female, they switch to her, and she flies them home.
There they eat her pollen, her nectar, and her egg. All from one fake date.

description:
In California's Mojave Desert, the larvae of the blister beetle Meloe franciscanus climb a plant stem and cluster into a clump of 120 to more than 2,000.
The clump gives off chemicals that copy the sex pheromone of a female digger bee. A male bee lands on it, the larvae attach to him within two seconds, and they move to a real female when he mates. She carries them to her nest, where they eat the pollen, the nectar and the bee's egg. The study was published in PNAS in 2006.
Smartest trick or meanest trick in the insect world? Comment below.
first_comment: A 2018 follow-up found the larvae tune their fake scent to the local bee species. Which animal con artist should we cover next?
